title: Agitated on pressure support ventilation
summary: A 71-year-old intubated patient with obstructive lung disease becomes agitated, with the bedside nurse reporting that the patient is fighting the ventilator.

evidence.claim: Ineffective triggering is the most frequent form of patient-ventilator dyssynchrony in COPD and is primarily driven by dynamic hyperinflation and auto-PEEP creating an inspiratory threshold load.
evidence.source: Thille AW, et al. Patient-ventilator asynchrony during assisted mechanical ventilation. Intensive Care Med 2006;32(10):1515-1522

evidence.claim: Applying extrinsic PEEP up to 70-80% of auto-PEEP reduces the work of triggering and ineffective efforts in spontaneously breathing patients with airflow obstruction without increasing total PEEP or lung volume.
evidence.source: Blanch L, et al. Measurement of air trapping, intrinsic positive end-expiratory pressure, and dynamic hyperinflation in mechanically ventilated patients. Minerva Anestesiol 2005;71(6):291-296

evidence.claim: Increasing the expiratory trigger cycling percentage (e.g. to 40-50% of peak inspiratory flow) shortens inspiratory time, reduces air trapping, and diminishes ineffective triggering in obstructive patients on PSV.
evidence.source: Chao DC, et al. Patient-ventilator trigger asynchrony in prolonged mechanical ventilation. Chest 1997;112(6):1592-1599

evidence.claim: Administering sedatives or opioids to treat dyssynchrony without correcting mechanical causes worsens hypoventilation and prolongs mechanical ventilation.
evidence.source: Kress JP, et al. Daily interruption of sedative infusions in critically ill patients undergoing mechanical ventilation. N Engl J Med 2000;342(20):1471-1477

evidence.claim: Acceptable gas exchange without significant respiratory acidosis, and no signs of fatigue, are among the criteria for tolerating reduced ventilator support.
evidence.source: Boles JM, et al. Weaning from mechanical ventilation. Eur Respir J 2007;29(5):1033-1056

evidence.claim: Boles 2007 wording checked: the consensus lists respiratory acidosis (pH below about 7.32) and signs of fatigue among the criteria for failing reduced support; it does not set pH above 7.30 as an endpoint.
evidence.source: Verified by reasoning from established clinical knowledge; not located in the local textbooks

patient.presentingStory: Intubated 3 days ago for a severe COPD exacerbation. Has been progressing well and was transitioned from assist-control to Pressure Support Ventilation (PSV) 2 hours ago. The nurse calls because he appears increasingly distressed, tachycardic, and diaphoresis has developed. The nurse asks: 'Can we sedate him? He is really fighting the vent.'
patient.history: Severe COPD with baseline FEV1 35% predicted. Home oxygen 2 L/min. Coronary artery disease with previous PCI 5 years ago. Quit smoking 4 years ago.

orderEffects.note: Sedative administration suppresses respiratory drive without solving mechanical dyssynchrony

actions.text: The patient is now heavily sedated and barely breathing spontaneously. Monitored minute ventilation drops markedly, and SpO2 is falling.
Scant clear secretions cleared from endotracheal tube. Breath-stacking and patient-ventilator mismatch persist.

findings.examine: Awake, diaphoretic, and distressed. Patient is using scalene and sternocleidomastoid accessory muscles. On physical inspection of the chest and abdomen, inward chest contractions and abdominal muscle tensing occur at a rate of ~26/min, but the ventilator breath indicator only flashes at ~13-14 bpm. Soft expiratory wheezing heard bilaterally.
findings.cxr: Endotracheal tube 4 cm above carina. Bilateral hyperinflated lung fields with flattened diaphragmatic domes. Blunting of costophrenic angles consistent with pleural thickening. No pneumothorax, pulmonary oedema, or acute focal pneumonia.

then.detail: Sedating a patient experiencing ineffective triggering blunts respiratory drive and causes severe hypoventilation without addressing the auto-PEEP threshold load.
Excessive pressure support increases tidal volume (> 9 mL/kg PBW), worsening dynamic hyperinflation and increasing ineffective efforts.

then.text: The patient looks much calmer and is breathing comfortably in sync with the ventilator. Every effort is triggering appropriately.

then.reason: Ventilator synchrony restored: extrinsic PEEP counterbalanced auto-PEEP, cycle-off criterion shortened late inspiration, and ineffective efforts were eliminated.

then.text: The patient is completely exhausted, diaphoresis is severe, and ABG shows worsening acidemia and carbon dioxide retention.

then.reason: Severe uncorrected patient-ventilator dyssynchrony resulted in diaphragmatic muscle fatigue and ventilatory failure.

then.text: Doctor, he looks tired and he's fighting the ventilator. Can you come and look?
He looks calmer and seems to be breathing more comfortably with the machine. I'll keep watching him.

predictionPoints.question: You optimize PSV settings by increasing PEEP (e.g. from 4 to 8 cmH2O) to offset auto-PEEP, raising cycle-off percentage to 40%, and adjusting flow trigger to 1.5 L/min. Over the next 15 minutes, which direction will each parameter move?
predictionPoints.explanation: Counterbalancing intrinsic PEEP with extrinsic PEEP reduces the threshold work needed to trigger a breath, so previously wasted efforts now trigger the ventilator (monitored rrTotal rises to match the patient's spontaneous rate). Raising expiratory cycle percentage terminates inspiration earlier, prolonging expiration, reducing trapped gas (autoPeep falls) and slightly decreasing tidal volume.

predictionPoints.question: What is the primary physiological mechanism causing ineffective triggering in this patient on pressure support ventilation?
options: Intrinsic PEEP creates an inspiratory threshold load that patient efforts cannot overcome to reach the trigger threshold
The endotracheal tube is occluded by a large mucus plug preventing any pressure sensing
Severe central nervous system depression has caused complete phrenic nerve cessation
The inspiratory valve is cycling off prematurely due to a massive circuit leak
predictionPoints.answerKey: Intrinsic PEEP creates an inspiratory threshold load that patient efforts cannot overcome to reach the trigger threshold
predictionPoints.explanation: When auto-PEEP is present, alveolar pressure remains positive at end-expiration. The patient must contract inspiratory muscles hard enough to lower alveolar pressure below external PEEP by the trigger sensitivity before the ventilator can detect the breath. If the effort is weak or auto-PEEP is high, the effort fails to trigger (ineffective effort).

rubric.description: Increased external PEEP to 7-9 cmH2O to offset auto-PEEP
Adjusted cyclePctPeakFlow to >= 35% to prevent delayed cycling
Avoided sedating an agitated patient whose agitation was due to patient-ventilator dyssynchrony
Administered bronchodilator to reduce airway resistance
Assessed blood gas to confirm adequate alveolar ventilation

keyPoints: In mechanically ventilated patients with obstructive airway disease on PSV, ineffective triggering is often mistaken for agitation or fighting the ventilator.
The cause is dynamic hyperinflation and auto-PEEP: the patient must generate muscle pressure exceeding intrinsic PEEP just to trigger a breath.
Sedating the patient treats the symptom and worsens the pathophysiology by blunting drive and leading to hypoventilation or apnoea.

The physiological solution is to add extrinsic PEEP (up to 70-80% of auto-PEEP) to offload the trigger threshold load, and raise the expiratory cycle threshold (e.g. 40-50% peak flow) to avoid delayed cycling.
